meta.title: Operation of Ultrasonic Cleaner in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To clean laboratory glassware, instruments, and botanical extraction vessels thoroughly using ultrasonic cavitation, and to assist in sonication-based extraction of phytochemicals from plant materials.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for cleaning resin-contaminated glassware, soaking plant material for enhanced extraction, and degassing solvents.
procedure: Fill the ultrasonic cleaner tank with the appropriate liquid: distilled water with 1–2% laboratory detergent for glassware cleaning; extraction solvent (e.g., ethanol, methanol) for sonication-assisted extraction.
Do not fill above the maximum fill line marked on the tank.
Switch on the unit and allow it to reach the set operating temperature if temperature control is available (typically 40–60°C for cleaning; room temperature for extraction).
For glassware cleaning: submerge items fully in the cleaning solution using the provided basket — do not place glassware directly on the tank bottom.
For sonication extraction: place the sample and solvent in a sealed conical flask or tube and submerge in the water bath — do not place open vessels of organic solvents directly in the tank.
Set the timer for the required duration: 10–20 minutes for glassware cleaning; 20–30 minutes for sonication extraction.
Switch on the ultrasonic transducers — you will hear a distinctive buzzing/hissing sound and see surface agitation.
At the end of the cycle, switch off and carefully remove items — tank contents may be hot.
Rinse cleaned glassware three times with fresh distilled water to remove detergent residues.
Allow glassware to drain and dry on a clean drying rack.
For extraction: filter the sonicated mixture immediately through a Buchner funnel or Whatman filter paper.
Drain and clean the tank after use — do not leave dirty solution in the tank.
Wipe the outer surface of the unit and cover when not in use.
Log usage: date, operator, material processed, solution used, and duration.
precautions: Never operate the ultrasonic cleaner without liquid in the tank — dry running destroys the transducers.
Do not use flammable organic solvents directly in the tank — the electrical components can ignite vapours; always use an indirect method (sealed flask inside water bath).
Do not submerge glassware with ground glass joints in hot alkaline solutions — etching damages the joints.
Do not place hands in the tank during operation — ultrasonic cavitation causes tissue damage.
Ensure the tank liquid level is always above the minimum level line.
Do not use strong acids or caustic solutions in the tank — they corrode the stainless steel tank.
Replace the cleaning solution when it becomes visibly contaminated — dirty solution reduces cleaning efficiency.
Drain and clean the tank weekly when in regular use.
